# The @atlas annotation block: is this moment mine?

## What this region is

The annotation every file carries: the @atlas block's axes and their rules, the comment syntax it is written in per language, and the patcher that writes and resyncs blocks from the repo's stamp rules.

## What it exists for

- Read or inspect a file's @atlas block from library code
- Decide what goes on a file's @uses line
- Write a file's block by hand
- Work out which comment syntax a file uses
- Place a new block correctly in a file
- Write or refresh @atlas blocks across files

## When this is not your domain

These mention this region's words but belong elsewhere; the answer is no, and the region named answers instead.

- add a new feature concept so files can be tagged with it → setup-and-config
- stop atlas from looking at the generated folder → setup-and-config
- fail the PR when a file has no block or names an unknown concept → validation-and-ci
- show the agent which concepts a file belongs to when it opens it → agent-integration
- list every file that is part of billing → map-outputs
